payload.description:
## Trigger

When coding agents work in parallel, I want worktrees that are commissioned, used and decommissioned by one agent-agnostic process, so I can parallelize, merge and see all work safely and fast.

## Owner rules (2026-10-07)

1. Working with worktrees is agnostic of the coding agent.
2. Worktrees live in a sibling folder of the repository, at the same level as the repository folder.
3. Worktrees are never inside the repository (for example under .claude), because they interfere with the CI gates.
4. Worktrees enable a high level of parallel work.
5. A worktree is commissioned, worked in, and decommissioned (deleted and cleaned up) when its work is complete.
6. A worktree lives only until its work is merged back into the branch that created it (usually main, possibly another feature branch).
7. Worktree work is secure, stable, transparent and fast.

The harness needs solid parallelization, merging, transparency, orchestration, coordination, idempotency and agent agnosticity.

## Evidence (measured 2026-10-07)

- git worktree list: 11 live harness worktrees; git merge-base --is-ancestor shows 9 of 11 branches already merged into main and never decommissioned (rule 5, rule 6).
- basicly worktree create refused: concurrency cap reached (11/10 live), so parallel work stopped (rule 4).
- Claude Code auto-mode denied basicly worktree cleanup of two merged, clean worktrees as irreversible local destruction, so decommissioning needs a manual permission (rule 5, rule 7).
- The sibling folder is named basicly.worktrees; the owner wrote <repo>.worktree. Confirm the name (rule 2).
- Memory note: the Agent tool isolation:worktree checks out inside the repository and poisons whole-tree gates (rule 3); basicly worktree bg-isolation exists for it.
payload.requirements:
- Audit src/basicly/worktree.py, the worktree-isolation skill and the loop landing against each of the seven rules, and record a pass or fail with evidence per rule.
- Keep refusal of unmerged or dirty worktrees; never delete unmerged work.
- No dependency changes.
